findings.detail: This is an operator-attested criterion requiring a concrete attestation that the mutation was seeded and the test was driven RED. The ticket comment (by RebarBotNava) provides a detailed runtime investigation but reports the OPPOSITE outcome: 'a seeded unconditional-stamp mutation left the test GREEN.' The comment explains two independently sufficient reasons why `clear_absent` is never reached on a healthy in-window pass, making it structurally impossible for this integration test to go RED from that mutation. No attestation in the ticket snapshot confirms the criterion was met (test driven RED). The comment explicitly states 'AC#2 is NOT satisfiable through this integration test.'
findings.remediation: Either (a) accept AC#1 hardening + the existing unit-tier guard as sufficient and formally drop/reclassify AC#2 in the ticket, or (b) if an integration-tier mutation-RED is still required, extend the test harness to wire the fake into the Backend port and add an out-of-window fixture so the bound-but-absent-alive path executes — then record a ticket comment with the specific mutation applied, the test run output showing RED, and the timestamp/run reference.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
